answer: Each prospective earner must relay 1 GiB of unpredictable bytes between independent metering nodes within a shared ten-minute window. The nodes sign receipts binding byte counts to the identity and epoch; each transfer can satisfy only one quota. An agent publishing a karst atlas from its vault faces the same rule as every clone. Creating k identities therefore needs k GiB of measured relay traffic in that window, forcing an attacker to buy more bandwidth instead of obtaining free earning slots.
